III.About

My path into digital humanities began with travel. For years I explored museums and historic sites on my own, in New York, across Ireland and Britain, through France, the Low Countries, Germany, Denmark, Italy, Spain and Portugal, and through most of the provinces of China. I read history as I went, and more than once I followed a single line in an old text up a mountain to look for what remained of a temple.

Each time I wondered how these places and objects, and the stories behind them, could reach more people. Digital humanities gave me the methods to pursue that question: rigorous research practice, critical thinking about tools and data, and the technical skills to build.

I hold an MA in Digital Humanities from University College Cork (2026) and a BA in Performing Arts from Nanjing Agricultural University (2021). Theatre taught me how space, pacing and attention shape what an audience experiences, and that training still informs how I design interactive work. Before my MA, I spent three years at Jiangsu Broadcasting Corporation running brand accounts, producing video and studying audience data, learning what makes people stay with a piece of content and what makes them move on. I bring that attention to every interactive piece I build.
